About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Digital Media Years 12–13 of the
New Zealand Curriculum. Equivalent for Te Marautanga o Aotearoa is being
published separately.

Progress and assessment information for Digital Media Years 12–13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Digital Media Years 12–13 is proposed to be
made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under section
90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Digital Media Years 12–13 will be required to start using it in Year 12 from
1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

  Students are taught technological practice, design thinking, and reflective
  development processes to create fit-for-purpose digital media outcomes. They
  are also taught project and file management, research and analysis skills, and
  how to design, build, test, and refine digital outcomes, with an understanding of
  ethical and societal considerations.

Through the study of Digital Media, students are taught how digital media can be
used to communicate information, experiences, and ideas through interactive,
information, and time-based media. They are taught how design principles,
conventions, user experience, technical production processes, and responsible
practices influence the development of digital media outcomes.

Digital Media provides students with the knowledge and practices to design, develop,
test, and evaluate digital media outcomes. Students apply this knowledge when
developing outcomes for users, audiences, and communities, using feedback and
evidence to inform design decisions and refinements.

As students progress through Years 12–13 Digital Media, they extend their
understanding of project management, digital design, technical production, and
responsible practice. They learn how digital media outcomes are shaped by technical,
cultural, ethical, and user considerations, and how evidence can be used to justify
design decisions and evaluate fitness for purpose.

  Digital media leads to pathways in screen industries, web and app development,
  creative technologies, interactive media, animation, and game development.

 Disciplinary writing

 Focus: the use of writing to reflect the ways in which knowledge is organised, analysed, and communicated within Digital Media.

 In Digital Media, writing is an analytical and reflective practice that enables students to explain and evaluate how design, technical development, interaction, and user or audience considerations
 shape digital media outcomes.
